links.note: Was 24095 Shaping public opinion and access to welfare. 'Which of the following is a pressure group?' belongs to Popular Struggles and Movements, a chapter with NO row anywhere in standard 43. None of Political Parties' 17 concepts covers pressure groups.

Was 24095. Asks which stated distinction between pressure groups and political parties is false. The pressure-group/party comparison lives in Popular Struggles and Movements; this chapter's set has no pressure-group concept, so the party side alone cannot carry the item.
Was 24091 Partisanship and ideology. Cochabamba is the Bolivian city of the water war - Popular Struggles and Movements. Nothing about party ideology is involved.
Was 24096 One-party system. 'Which king of Nepal refused to accept democratic rule' is the Nepal movement in Popular Struggles and Movements. A monarch is not a party system.
Was 24095. 'Not true about the pressure groups' - Popular Struggles and Movements; no pressure-group concept exists in this chapter.
Was 24102 Dynastic succession and money power. 'When did Nepal first win democracy' is the Nepal case in Popular Struggles and Movements, unrelated to dynastic party leadership.

Was 24088 Parties and the rise of democracy. Keys 'None of above' to establish that political parties, pressure groups AND movement groups are all agencies of organised politics - the three-way classification in Popular Struggles and Movements. Two of the three have no concept here, so the item cannot sit on a Political Parties concept.

Was 24089 Parties as vehicles of federal sharing. Keys 'popular struggles' to 'most of the time democracy evolves through ___' - the opening claim of Popular Struggles and Movements. Federal power sharing is not in the item.

Was 24087 Parties are recent in history. Asks which organisation did not join the protest movement (the Nepal SPA case) - Popular Struggles and Movements. The history of party formation is not involved.

Was 24090 What a political party is. 'Usually sectional interest groups seek to promote ___' is the sectional/public interest-group distinction in Popular Struggles and Movements, not the definition of a party.
Was 24095. 'Pressure groups and movements have deepened democracy by' - Popular Struggles and Movements' closing argument. No concept here covers pressure groups or movements.
Was 24088. The positive form of qid:105567, keying that parties, pressure groups and movements are all agencies of organised politics. Same reason.

Was 24096 One-party system. Keys India as the South Asian country democratic since independence; India is not a one-party state, so the link is simply wrong, and no concept in this chapter concerns a country's democratic record. The item belongs with the South Asia material in Outcomes of Democracy or Class 9's contemporary-democracy chapter.

Was 24088. 'Which of these values have the moral and legal sanctions in a democracy' is Outcomes of Democracy's dignity passage - I have linked the identical stem at qid:105646 in chapter 23714 to 24118. It should be re-chaptered to 23714, not held on a Political Parties concept.

Was 24096 One-party system. Keys 'Transparency' as the factor missing from non-democratic government - Outcomes of Democracy's accountable-government concept (24107 in chapter 23714). Nothing to do with party systems.
Was 24088. 'Democracies have successfully...' keyed to political inequality being rejected - Outcomes of Democracy, where I linked the same stem at qid:105653 to 24113. Belongs in 23714.

Was 24098 Multi-party system. Keys 'a democratic regime' as best suited to accommodate social diversity - the question is about regimes, not party systems, and it is Outcomes of Democracy's 24116. The words 'diverse society' in 24098's description are the only overlap.

Was 24088. Distribution of economic benefits in democracies (rich incomes rising, poor declining) is Outcomes of Democracy's 24114; I linked the identical stem at qid:105656 in 23714. Belongs in 23714.

Was 24088. 'Democracy is a better form of government because it:' is Outcomes of Democracy's 24105, already carrying the same stem at qid:105658 in 23714. No Political Parties concept is about comparing regimes.
